note: counts and totals of memory to import cover `kind: memory` only. An index file is a pointer list and a `claude` entry is instructions -- read both for context, import neither as a fact. A memory file is flagged in `over_max_text` above 1800 chars, not 2000: remember appends --keywords into the same field the 2000-char CHECK counts, so 200 chars are reserved for them and each entry's `reason` says which limit it hit. Split or condense such a file, never truncate it. Nothing is skipped silently: report `unreadable` (unreadable file or directory, broken symlink, symlink loop), `excluded_dirs` (protected subdirectory of a memory root) and `empty` (nothing to import -- the writer refuses an empty --text) as gaps. `nothing_to_do` is true only when there is nothing to import AND nothing was skipped; do not derive that verdict from `n_memory_files` alone.
